items.title: November 11 general strike adds to rail disruption
items.body: Renfe drivers strike on November 10 and 12 over unresolved safety commitments; a wider rail stoppage is threatened for November 17. The November 11 general strike also affects flights and public services. Minimum rail services include 75% of rush-hour Cercanías trains, 50% off-peak, and 73% of high-speed and long-distance trains.

items.title: Court preserves voting rights for citizenship recipients' children
items.body: The Supreme Court rejected requests to suspend voting rights for 189,678 children of Ley de Nietos citizenship recipients in the November 29 election. It said changing the overseas register now would undermine electoral stability. The suspension affecting 162,454 recipients remains; the main case is pending.

items.title: Toledo Cathedral hosts funeral for Urda rail victims
items.body: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia attend a funeral Mass for the 69 victims of the Urda rail accident at Toledo Cathedral on November 10 at 19.00. The ceremony follows an earlier funeral in Urda on October 31. At the cathedral, 69 candles represent those killed.

items.title: Retirement at 65 requires longer contributions from January
items.body: Under the 2013 pension reform, retirement at 65 will require 38 years and 6 months of contributions from January 1, 2027; otherwise, the age will be 67. In 2026, the thresholds are 38 years and 3 months, or age 66 years and 10 months. This final step responds to longer lives and an ageing population.

items.title: Canary Islands seek extra migration reception support
items.body: Canary Islands president Fernando Clavijo seeks central government approval for a migration contingency plan after more than 7,000 irregular arrivals in November. It would expand rescue, reception, and transfers. The islands care for 2,950 unaccompanied minors against 737 places; all regional parliamentary groups except Vox back the plan.

items.title: Sánchez plans extra cabinet meeting before election
items.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has announced plans for at least one extraordinary cabinet meeting before the November 29 election. It would address pending social measures, but he gave no details. He also repeated his intention to approve a pardon for former attorney general Álvaro García Ortiz.

items.title: First Lyme disease vaccine under European review
items.body: The European Medicines Agency is evaluating Pfizer and Valneva's Lyme disease vaccine, which showed efficacy above 70% in trials. Approval is still pending, and results await peer-reviewed publication. It could protect people exposed to ticks through outdoor activities, particularly in northern Spain.

items.title: Spain's tax burden reaches 38.1% of GDP
items.body: Spain's taxes and social contributions reached 38.1% of GDP in 2025, up 0.9 points, Eurostat figures show. Revenue grew faster than the economy, while a strong labour market raised social contributions. The burden remained below the EU's 40.7% and the eurozone's 41.2%; some data is provisional.

items.title: Electric car grants could run out in November
items.body: Spain's Auto+ vehicle grants remain in force until December 31, but sector sources expect funds to run out around the November 29 election. Applications from individuals had reached 305.6 million euros against a 350 million budget. Support for 2027 remains undecided, leaving prospective buyers facing uncertainty.

items.title: CaixaBank forecasts slower growth and easing inflation
items.body: CaixaBank Research forecasts Spain's economy will grow 2% in 2027, down from 2.6% in 2026 but above the eurozone's 1.4%. It expects inflation to fall from 3.4% at the end of 2026 to 2.5% in 2027. Population growth supports the expansion, while weak productivity and a housing shortage remain concerns.

items.title: PP proposes electricity tax cuts and social tariff
items.body: Partido Popular leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo's election programme proposes scrapping the 7% electricity generation tax and cutting taxes on electricity use. A single social tariff would replace electricity and heating bonuses and cover free-market contracts too. The pledges depend on the PP winning the November 29 election.
